clue.text: See 4
See 4
Unbeliever gets little change from Indian mystic

indicators.note: a little change means a small alteration to the mystic's word, here two letters trading places

parts.note: a fakir is a Hindu or Muslim holy man living on alms

explanation.surface: A sceptic is short-changed by an Indian holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'little change' is just the first and third letters of the mystic trading places.
explanation.definitionFit: Kafir is an Arabic-derived term used for someone who rejects Islam, hence an infidel.

clue.text: Clue not used for bat

indicators.note: something used is worn and knocked about, so the letters lose their original order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter complains that a perfectly good clue was rejected for the word bat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is self-referential: the clue it claims was not used is in fact the clue in front of you.
explanation.definitionFit: The noctule is a large brown European species of the flying mammal, so it is an example.

clue.text: Araucaria in May, reportedly tied in with dynamite in Welsh river, displays sign about fellow that volunteers knowledge, having chewed the fat with John Duke: Shed holds a medal for musical composition: let's go!

indicators.note: in tells us the setter's pronoun goes inside the politician's first name

parts.note: Theresa May, the Conservative politician, supplies her first name THERESA
the setter referring to himself, so the first-person pronoun I

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard rather than as written, so the following words count by their sound

parts.note: said aloud, these two words sound like the sea's rise coming in, TIDE IN

indicators.note: in again tells us one piece sits within the other, the explosive inside the river

parts.note: the Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff
HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive
displays, in the sense of shows off, means airs

indicators.note: about means going round, so the sign wraps round the fellow

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come
which can stand in for that as a relative pronoun
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
ken means knowledge or range of understanding

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters of the words that follow are jumbled

parts.note: the john is slang for a toilet, a loo

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the shed has the medal inside it

parts.note: a lean-to is a shed built against a wall; Shed is also a fellow Guardian setter
the DSO, Distinguished Service Order, is a military medal
a tune is a short musical composition

explanation.surface: A rambling account of the setter's day: rivers, explosives, a chat with John, a medal in a shed, then off we go.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the line from Julius Caesar. 'Chewed' jumbles THE FAT into AT THE F. LOO and D complete the flood; LEAN-TO 'holds' DSO; FOR and TUNE finish it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus's speech urges seizing the moment before the chance ebbs away, a call to act now, much like a rallying cry to set off.

clue.text: Tennis player entertains the rash guy

indicators.note: a host who entertains has guests inside the house, so one word sits within another

parts.note: Lew Hoad, the Australian Wimbledon champion of the 1950s
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tennis star plays host to some reckless fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead is an impetuous person who acts without thinking, which is what being rash means.

clue.text: Paucity of new characters in heraldic form

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the heraldic word

parts.note: a fess is a broad horizontal band across a heraldic shield

indicators.note: only the characters of the word are used, not their order, so they can be rearranged

parts.note: the letters of new rearranged

explanation.surface: A shortage of fresh symbols in a coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: A fess is a term from heraldry, the design of coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Paucity and fewness both mean a smallness of number or a scarcity, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Cart sinful love up to source of oil

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads, as used by brewers
wicked, sinful
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A wicked passion drives someone towards an oil well, or so the picture runs.
explanation.definitionFit: An olive grove yields the fruit that is pressed to make oil, so it is a supplier of that commodity.

clue.text: Denials of personality, hence Hain is not amused

indicators.note: hence means derived from this, so the answer is made out of the following letters

parts.note: taken as written; Peter Hain was a Labour cabinet minister

explanation.surface: A politician, Peter Hain, takes offence at being treated as less than human.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no conventional anagram word: the whole phrase after 'hence' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Dehumanisation strips people of their individual human qualities, so each instance refuses them a personality.

clue.text: Working well with fence — if it works

indicators.note: works suggests the letters are worked over and put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says a fence is doing its job, provided it actually functions.
explanation.definitionFit: An efficient machine or person performs with little waste of effort, which is functioning productively.

clue.text: See 4
See 4
Glance at metal girder (say with the other I?)

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken, and the other I is the sound-alike spelling of the letter

parts.note: an I-beam is a steel girder whose cross-section looks like a capital I

explanation.surface: A builder eyes a steel joist, puzzling over its shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter I and the organ of sight are pronounced the same, so swapping one for the other leaves the sound unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-beam is an old poetic word for a look or ray from the eye, so it means a quick look.

clue.text: Friday's little ones missing mount

indicators.note: missing means the young ones are taken away from the day of the week

parts.note: the day of the week
fry are young fish, and by extension small children

explanation.surface: Children absent on a Friday, or Man Friday's offspring gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters F, R and Y are scattered through the day rather than together, but all three come out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is a mountain in Crete, and another near Troy, both famous from Greek myth.

clue.text: Laurel's first got into supreme predicament without point

parts.note: A1, first-class, written with I for one

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a mess is a difficult situation

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the comedian's name

parts.note: Stan Laurel of Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: Laurel, of Laurel and Hardy, lands in yet another fine mess, to no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy's catchphrase was 'another fine mess', which the surface borrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless describes something lacking purpose or direction, which is having no point to it.

clue.text: Dinner without starter: meat eater gets thin round cut

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the meal goes round its starter

parts.note: a dinner is a meal
the starter of dinner is its first letter
the lion is a carnivore

explanation.surface: A diner skips the first course while a carnivore gets a dainty slice of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dinner without starter' looks like dropping the first letter, giving INNER; instead the meal wraps round its own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a small round slice of meat such as beef or pork, so it is a cut.

clue.text: Give cards, mostly in pouch

indicators.note: mostly means all but a bit, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to give someone their cards is British slang for firing them, returning their employment papers

explanation.surface: Dealing out playing cards from a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cards' suggests a card game; 'give someone their cards' is the British idiom for dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sac is a bag-like cavity in a plant or animal, which is a pouch in anatomy.

clue.text: "Diamonds" said wrongly in scorn

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of said are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone who wrongly said 'Diamonds' at the card table is held in scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word joining the definition, but it is the last piece of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain and scorn are synonyms, both meaning contempt for something thought unworthy.

clue.text: Diamonds are cold

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for gems, especially diamonds

definitions.note: adjective, whereas the answer is a noun; something cold is like it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: frozen water, the epitome of coldness

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that diamonds are cold and heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds, and frozen water is the type of something chilly.

clue.text: Australian spider left behind

parts.note: a red is a left-winger, a socialist or communist
at the back, behind

explanation.surface: An Australian spider that has been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left behind' reads as one phrase meaning abandoned; it splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: The redback is a venomous Australian relative of the black widow, so it is an example.

clue.text: See 4
Sovereign for £1,000 in spirit for citadel

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: a gremlin is a mischievous imp blamed for mechanical faults
a grand is £1,000, abbreviated G
K is the abbreviation for king, a sovereign

explanation.surface: Swapping a gold coin for a thousand pounds within a spirit, as if at a money changer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sovereign looks like the gold coin, worth a pound, which fits the money theme; here it is a king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortified complex at the heart of Moscow, and a kremlin is any Russian city fortress.

clue.text: Inflamed and awfully sore externally behind the altar

definitions.note: a phrase of place, whereas the answer is a noun for the screen there

indicators.note: externally means on the outside, so these letters wrap round the other piece
awfully suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: the letters of sore rearranged
red and sore, as inflamed skin is

explanation.surface: A sore patch that is red and inflamed, oddly located behind an altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or panel standing at the back of a church altar.

clue.text: Second half beginning with the others' skill

parts.note: the rest are the others
an art is a skill

explanation.surface: The second half kicks off with the opposing team showing their skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A match resumes after half-time with a fresh kick-off, a resumption of play after the interval.

clue.text: Tear off toes in retort

parts.note: to tear is to rip

indicators.note: off means out of sorts or wrong, so the letters go out of order

parts.note: the letters of toes rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bites someone's toes off in a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick sharp reply, originally a fencer's counter-thrust, so a comeback.

clue.text: Wish I hadn't a plant?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a bitter-leaved evergreen herb

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as regret at having planted something; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue an action is to regret having done it, and rue is also a strong-smelling medicinal herb.

clue.text: Wearing specs, perhaps, have debts and finish back inside

indicators.note: inside places the turned-round word within the other piece

parts.note: to owe is to be in debt

indicators.note: back means the word for finish is read from right to left

parts.note: to finish someone off is to kill them

explanation.surface: A spectacled person who is broke and on the point of giving up.
explanation.walkthrough: Owls are pictured with big round eyes, so glasses give someone an owlish look.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles make a person look like the round-eyed night bird, so wearing them may give that appearance.

clue.text: Wise guy's concession to some of the past

parts.note: a sop is a small concession to placate someone

indicators.note: some of means only part of the word is used, the rest dropped

parts.note: history is the past

explanation.surface: A clever fellow makes a small allowance for bits of history.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophist is a clever but specious reasoner, originally a paid teacher of wisdom in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Pub with sex appeal, n'est ce pas?

parts.note: an inn is a pub
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A pub with plenty of allure, don't you agree?
explanation.walkthrough: Innit is a British slang contraction of 'isn't it', used as an all-purpose question tag.
explanation.definitionFit: The French tag n'est-ce pas works exactly like the slang tag, inviting agreement at a sentence's end.

clue.text: One in prison has corn

indicators.note: in places the one inside the prison's name

parts.note: the Maze was a high-security prison in Northern Ireland
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prisoner has a supply of grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is the cereal plant called corn in North America, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: See 4
Nearly half the tennis in two northeastern forms

indicators.note: forms means the letters are formed into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
NE, the compass abbreviation for northeast, twice

explanation.surface: Nearly half the tennis played in the northeast takes two shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine nineteenths is a fraction just short of one half, since half of nineteen is nine and a half.
